A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SigNet research and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. The comparison includes v2's supplementary Sections 6–7; much of their setup information appears in v1's main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original SigNet results on four datasets in Table 1, component and fusion ablations in Table 3 and Figure 8, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds density comparisons, decomposition-path ablations, and additional visual examples, including supplementary Figure 10.

M1.justification: The densification, denoising, degradation estimation, DADF decomposition, conditional Mamba, and training losses remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and Equations (1)–(14) are retained. The new discussion explains the existing three-path choice without establishing a changed inference procedure.

E1.justification: The four main datasets and KITTI failure analysis remain. v2 adds input-sparsity scenarios at 1%, 5%, 35%, 65%, and 95% density. Their dataset attribution is inconsistent: Table 2 names TOFDC, while Section 4.1.3 names DIML.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains identical comparator membership for each dataset, and the existing visual comparisons retain their baselines. The added density comparison uses the already evaluated TPVD; supplementary comparisons reuse CSPN and AGG-Net.

E3.justification: v2 introduces evaluation configurations covering five input densities and decomposition-path counts of 3, 5, 7, 9, and 11. The retained benchmark splits, resolutions, metrics, and training budget remain as reported in v1. The density-sampling and retraining procedures are not specified.

E4.justification: New Tables 2 and 4 examine sensitivity to input density and decomposition-path count. v2 also adds degradation examples, a second KITTI failure example, and supplementary DIML comparisons. Existing component, Mamba, and iteration ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added experiments continue reporting individual point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the retained ablation scores are unchanged. New Table 2 reports, for example, 144.6 for SigNet versus 156.6 for TPVD at 1% density. Table 4 reports RMSE decreasing from 55.0 to 54.0 mm across three to eleven paths. Additional qualitative results are also supplied.

T1.justification: The degradation assumptions, mathematical formulation, and loss definitions remain equivalent. Metric definitions move from v1 Table 2 to supplementary Table 5 without mathematical changes. No new theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same claims about completion as enhancement, eliminating mismatch and ambiguity, degradation-guided fusion, and state-of-the-art performance. The shortened experimental contribution bullet preserves its original meaning.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the density results as evidence of generalization across valid-point densities and explains retaining three decomposition paths as a computational tradeoff. The indoor/near-range applicability boundary and explanations for KITTI failures remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Supplementary Section 6.3 newly lists flipping among training augmentations and specifies the GPU as an NVIDIA RTX 3090. Most setup details are relocated from v1 rather than newly supplied. The PDFs do not establish whether flipping reflects changed training or additional disclosure.

R1.justification: v2 adds four introductory references concerning adverse-weather optical flow, LiDAR object detection, and Voxelsplat, while shortening some related-work summaries. The central positioning relative to depth completion and degradation learning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the experimental documentation: dataset, metric, and implementation subsections move into supplementary Section 6, followed by a new visualization section. Related-work and method headings are streamlined, and substantial portions of their explanatory prose are condensed or rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds two experimental tables and Figure 10, expands degradation and KITTI visual panels, and redraws method diagrams. The complexity chart switches from FPS labels to reciprocal latency and corrects its bubble-size description. Table 1 changes highlighting, and metric definitions move into the supplement.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity tests and successful/failure-case visuals modestly strengthen empirical support for the existing design. The corrected complexity-chart description also improves clarity. However, the new density experiment inconsistently names TOFDC and DIML and provides limited protocol detail. These weaknesses constrain the gains; the core method and headline results remain unchanged.
